lines: Jordan Lee
+1 (555) 010-2468 | jordan.lee@example.com | example.com/code/jordan-lee
Date of birth: 14 Mar 1999 | Nationality: Canadian
EDUCATION
Western State University | M.S. in Computer Engineering | Metro City, USA | Sep 2024 - Expected Jun 2026
Eastern Institute of Technology | B.S. in Electrical Engineering | Metro City, Country | Sep 2018 - Jun 2022
EXPERIENCE
Lakeside Auto Parts | Mechanical Design Engineer | Metro City, Country | Jun 2025 - Present
- Designed stamping dies for automotive brackets in SolidWorks, cutting the scrap rate from 6% to 4% on two press lines.
- Ran tolerance stack-up analyses for 12 production parts and signed off first-article inspections with the supplier.
Mobility Systems Company | Machine Learning Engineering Intern | Metro City, USA | Oct 2024 - May 2025
- Improved diagnostic accuracy by 35% after fine-tuning a domain adapter on validated tool-use trajectories with assistant-only loss masking.
- Designed a routing layer that limits each of 3 specialist agents and an independent reviewer to their in-scope signals, cutting reviewer disagreement with specialist findings from 14% to 6%.

- Trained the triage agent with GRPO on grouped tool-use rollouts and a reward that penalises redundant calls, cutting tool calls per case 18% and end-to-end latency 5% versus the SFT baseline at equal accuracy.
- Wrote the evaluation harness the team used to compare 14 adapter checkpoints on accuracy, citation quality and latency, catching 2 accuracy regressions before release.
- Fine-tuned the adapter with assistant-only loss masking so the model would learn to reproduce the tool outputs more faithfully.

- Built a diagnostics triage branch for an industrial inspection system that screens 800+ sensor signals per case with ML-extracted features, cutting the pending-case backlog 68% in the eight weeks after launch.
Eastern Robotics Co. | Junior Software Engineer | Metro City, Country | Aug 2022 - Jul 2024
- Cut GPU memory for fine-tuning the perception models by 4x by switching from FP32 to BF16 mixed precision.
- Reduced p95 API latency from 420 ms to 180 ms by adding a request cache and batching sensor reads, with load tests that fail the build if p95 exceeds 200 ms.
- Maintained the CI pipeline for the perception team's model releases and adds automated regression checks that shortened release cycles to 3 days.
- Migrated 30 robot-fleet services from cron jobs to an event queue with retries and dead-letter handling, removing the nightly backlogs that delayed morning dispatch.
PROJECTS
Agent Runtime Suite | Owner | TypeScript, Multi-Agent Systems | Aug 2025 - Present
- Drove adoption of AI-first engineering practices across the platform, accelerating delivery and improving outcomes for downstream teams.
- Kept working context under 10K tokens across a 100-turn stress test while the raw conversation grew 100x, using budgeted context layers and staged compaction.
- Separated concurrency pools and gated cache writes on stream completion, removing nested-pool deadlocks and lost tool results under 50-way fan-out.
Research-Agent Evaluation Framework | Contributor | LLM Evaluation | Feb 2025 - Jul 2025
- Integrated 8 citation and faithfulness metrics into an open-source research-agent framework's evaluation module.
- Showed the evaluator tracks injected degradation with a Kendall correlation of 0.89 across 400+ report-level trials that removed citations, sources and claims.
- Cut the pending-case backlog by two-thirds with a triage branch that screens 800+ sensor signals per case using ML-extracted features.
SKILLS
Programming: Python, TypeScript, Git
ML & Agents: PyTorch, LoRA, GRPO, agent evaluation

items.says: Remove the date of birth and nationality.
items.because: They are generally unnecessary on a North American resume and can introduce privacy and bias concerns.

items.says: Make the target role clearer and tailor which experience you emphasize.
items.because: The résumé spans mechanical design, robotics software, and ML/agents without making every experience equally central to a given application.

items.says: Ensure the code portfolio link leads directly to relevant, professional work.
Consider adding a LinkedIn profile.
items.because: It could support the application.

items.says: Clarify location or relocation status elsewhere if applying in a different country.
items.because: The university’s location may differ from the target role’s country.

items.says: Use a city-and-country location format consistent with the M.S. entry.
items.because: The two education entries use different location formats.

items.says: Clarify how the master’s program overlaps with employment.
items.because: The internship and current job overlap with the program, and the dates and locations could otherwise seem implausible.

items.says: Give context for the current mechanical-design role and make its employment arrangement clear.
items.because: It sits alongside a computer engineering master’s program and recent ML experience.

items.says: Clarify the scrap-rate measurement period or comparison basis.
items.because: Readers need that context to interpret the change.

items.says: Distinguish the percentage-point change from the relative reduction.
items.because: They describe the scrap-rate result differently.

items.says: Explain what the analyses or first-article sign-offs enabled or prevented.
items.because: The outcome is unclear despite the number of parts giving scope.

items.says: Make the responsibility in the supplier sign-off process precise.
Define the 35% accuracy increase and its supporting baseline, metric, and evaluation set.
items.because: Readers cannot tell whether the increase is relative or absolute or how it was evaluated.

items.says: Make the result understandable without assuming knowledge of the training setup.
items.because: “Validated tool-use trajectories” and “assistant-only loss masking” are specialized terms.

items.says: Explain how reviewer disagreement was measured and over what sample.
Explain why lower reviewer disagreement indicates improvement.
items.because: A lower disagreement rate is not automatically better.

items.says: Make the agents’ scope and “in-scope signals” more concrete.
Specify the benchmark, workload, and evaluation set behind “equal accuracy.”
items.because: The accuracy comparison needs to be meaningful for the same workload and evaluation set.

items.says: Clarify how calls per case and latency were measured.
items.because: The key evidence is spread across several clauses.

items.says: Define what counted as an accuracy regression.
Clarify whether the regressions were caught before deployment or release.
The assistant-only loss-masking technique repeats the first Mobility Systems bullet.
items.because: As written, it reads like the same work is being claimed twice.

items.says: Verify that the stated purpose describes what masking changed during training.
The backlog result is duplicated in the Research-Agent project.
items.because: The review says to keep the result in only the most appropriate place.

items.says: Clarify the backlog measurement period.
Explain how the triage branch contributed to the backlog reduction.
Explain the role of the ML-extracted features.
items.because: The phrase is broad unless readers can infer what the features did.

items.says: Clarify what “4x” means for the memory reduction.
items.because: It is unclear whether memory fell to one-quarter of its prior level.

items.says: Make the memory measurement and its attribution to the precision change defensible.
items.because: Switching from FP32 to BF16 alone may not explain a fourfold change in every setup.

items.says: Add the load-test conditions if they matter to interpreting the latency result.
Fix the switch from past tense to “adds.”
items.because: The other bullets describe completed work.

items.says: Define what a three-day release cycle measures and give the prior comparison point.
Quantify the effect of removing the nightly backlog or clarify its effect on morning dispatch.
Clarify your contribution if the migration was a team effort.
items.because: The bullet could imply you personally delivered the entire migration.

items.says: Substantiate the adoption and outcomes with concrete evidence or remove the bullet.
items.because: The claim is broad, difficult to verify, and less informative than the technical bullets.

items.says: State what the “100x” growth compares and how context size was measured.
Show evidence that the system remained useful, if available.
items.because: Staying within the token limit alone does not establish usefulness.

items.says: Clarify the test conditions behind “50-way fan-out.”
Explain how elimination of deadlocks and lost tool results was verified, if available.
Identify the framework or repository.
items.because: Readers need the project’s context to understand the contribution.

items.says: Clarify whether you implemented the metrics, connected existing ones, or both.
Identify the two measures in the Kendall correlation.
items.because: Readers need to interpret what the figure validates.

items.says: Explain how the 400-plus trials were constructed.
items.because: Readers need to interpret what the figure validates.

items.says: The sensor-triage backlog result duplicates the Mobility Systems result.
items.because: The review says to remove it from this project unless it was genuinely part of the project.

items.says: Clarify how the sensor-triage work belongs in this project, if it does.
items.because: It appears unrelated to the research-agent evaluation project.

items.says: Show relevant languages and tools supported by the experience.
items.because: The programming list is very short and does not show substantial systems, API, robotics, or design-software experience.

items.says: Replace broad labels with the specific methods, frameworks, and evaluation tools used in the bullets.
items.because: The current ML and agents entries are broad.
